caption_used: The performance of knowledge probing after editing with different editing methods on BioMedLM, where "Base" denotes LLM without editing. The x-axis shows co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale, while the y-axis represents accuracy (ACC %). All six methods show improving accuracy with increasing co-occurrence frequency. ROME consistently achieves the highest accuracy, starting at approximately 51% and reaching roughly 66% at the highest co-occurrence numbers. MEND and MEMIT follow as the next best performers, with MEND reaching approximately 56% and MEMIT approximately 55%. Notably, IKE demonstrates a steeper improvement rate than FT, surpassing it at co-occurrence numbers above 10^2 to reach approximately 52% at the highest frequency. The Base model exhibits the lowest performance throughout, plateauing at approximately 44%.

The plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC %) of knowledge probing after editing with six different methods on BioMedLM, as a function of co-occurrence number. The x-axis is a logarithmic scale, ranging from approximately 10^1 to 10^3, with tick labels spaced by powers of ten. The y-axis represents accuracy (ACC %) and ranges from approximately 40% to 66%, with tick labels spaced by 5%. A black solid line represents the Base model, which begins at approximately 44% and remains relatively constant at that value throughout the x-axis. A dark gray solid line represents the MEND method, starting at approximately 48% and increasing to approximately 56%. A light gray solid line represents the MEMIT method, beginning at approximately 51% and rising to approximately 55%. A turquoise solid line represents the FT method, starting at approximately 53% and increasing to approximately 58%. A red solid line represents the IKE method, beginning at approximately 45% and rising to approximately 52%. Finally, a maroon solid line represents the ROME method, starting at approximately 51% and reaching approximately 66% at the highest co-occurrence number.
